title: Industry 4.0 and the IIoT
welcome_lead: Cyber-physical systems, big data, and the connected factory.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: Industry 4.0, IIoT, and cyber-physical systems.

concepts.def: Fourth industrial revolution — cyber-physical, networked manufacturing.
Industrial Internet of Things — networked sensors and machines.
Physical machine integrated with computation and network.
Processing data close to source rather than in a central cloud.
Open Platform Communications standard for industrial data exchange.
Using sensor data to forecast failure before it occurs.

walkthroughs.body_html: Industry 1.0: steam (1780s). 2.0: electricity, mass production (1870s). 3.0: electronics, automation (1960s). 4.0: cyber-physical systems, IoT — coined at Hannover Messe, 2011.
The IIoT connects machines, sensors and SCADA via standards like OPC UA and MQTT. Edge computing reduces latency and cloud bandwidth by processing close to the machine.
Predictive maintenance uses vibration, temperature and acoustic sensors to forecast bearing or motor failure. Studies report 25-30% maintenance cost reduction over reactive approaches.
